### E1-3 Actions and resources in relation to climate policies

Subsea7’s climate actions support its target to reduce Scope 1 and Scope 2 greenhouse gas emissions by 50% by 2035, compared with a 2018 baseline, and to achieve net-zero greenhouse gas emissions by 2050. In 2023, the reported reduction target remained 50% of base-year emissions, including Scope 1 emissions.

Our action framework focuses on improving operational eco-efficiency, increasing renewable electricity procurement, developing lower-carbon solutions for clients and expanding capabilities serving renewable-energy markets. As vessel operations account for more than 90% of our emissions, operational initiatives principally address fuel use and vessel efficiency. Measures have included carbon and energy-saving initiatives and the use of selective catalytic reduction technology on new-build vessels, which reduces nitrogen oxide emissions by approximately 75%. Subsea7’s owned vessels are also enlisted in the Norwegian NOx Fund, through which member fees support the implementation of green technology in the shipping industry.

For onshore operations, we seek to use renewable electricity where available and monitor the percentage of sites supplied through renewable-energy tariffs. This reached 73% in 2022, compared with 66% in 2021. Operational energy-efficiency initiatives reported for 2022 reduced CO₂ emissions by 98,744 tonnes, saved 37,536 m³ of fuel and generated $31.0 million of operational cost savings.

Actions supporting the wider energy transition include using a carbon-estimator tool in tenders and studies, maintaining an energy-transition research and development programme and developing products, expertise and capabilities for lower-carbon and renewable-energy solutions. In 2022, 56% of the total research and development budget was associated with the energy transition. Renewable projects supported by Subsea7 had reached a cumulative power capacity of 10.5 GW by the end of 2022.

We also engage our value chain. More than 25 suppliers participated in a pilot greenhouse gas emissions questionnaire. The results and supplier feedback were intended to inform an action plan for sustainable procurement and the development of supplier-selection criteria.

Financial resources associated with climate-change mitigation are monitored through the EU Taxonomy. For 2022, taxonomy-aligned capital expenditure was $122 million and taxonomy-aligned operating expenditure was $17 million. Eligible capital expenditure and operating expenditure relate to the installation, maintenance and repair of renewable-energy technologies. The eligibility indicators are calculated using existing processes and reporting systems, including management assumptions, and are reported under the climate-change mitigation objective.

Oversight of climate-related developments has also been supported by a dedicated workgroup established to address the recommendations of the Task Force on Climate-related Financial Disclosures. Scenario analysis indicated that Subsea7’s strategic focus on lower-carbon oil and gas and renewable markets remained relevant across the pathways considered.
